title: ～はもちろん — “not to mention ～ / of course ～”
summary: Says that A is obvious, and goes on to add B, which is not so obvious: “A of course, and B too.” It follows a noun, and B is often marked with も. Used to stress how wide something extends.

patterns.form: 名詞A＋はもちろん、名詞B＋も
patterns.gloss: A of course, and B as well

patterns.form: 名詞A＋はもちろん（のこと）、…
patterns.gloss: A is a given (also written Aはもちろんのこと)

body.p: A is what everyone would expect; B is the surprising or wider addition. 英語はもちろん、フランス語も話せる: English is natural, and French too.
A is a noun (a verb needs の or こと). B usually has も or まで after it. The speaker stresses that the range reaches B as well, so both A and B are true.
～だけでなく～も is neutral. ～はもちろん treats A as too obvious to explain and so sounds more emphatic. Write it with the hiragana もちろん; it is the same word as the adverb “of course”.

examples.ja: 彼（かれ）は英語（えいご）はもちろん、フランス語（ご）も話（はな）せる。
examples.romaji: Kare wa eigo wa mochiron, furansugo mo hanaseru.
examples.tr: He can speak French, not to mention English.
examples.note: English is the given; French is the added surprise.

examples.ja: この公園（こうえん）は、子（こ）どもはもちろん、大人（おとな）にも人気（にんき）がある。
examples.romaji: Kono kouen wa, kodomo wa mochiron, otona ni mo ninki ga aru.
examples.tr: This park is popular with adults, not to mention children.

examples.ja: 週末（しゅうまつ）はもちろん、平日（へいじつ）もこの店（みせ）は混（こ）んでいる。
examples.romaji: Shuumatsu wa mochiron, heijitsu mo kono mise wa konde iru.
examples.tr: This shop is crowded on weekdays too, not to mention weekends.

pitfalls: A should really be the obvious one. Putting the surprising item first sounds wrong.
B normally needs も or まで. Dropping it makes the sentence feel unfinished.
